catalog.name: plugins_list
catalog.description: Read the plugin inventory: every discovered plugin (built-in and site-installed) with its id, name, version, source, trust tier, validation status, current enabled state, and any validation errors. Read-only. Also returns agentPlugins: every installed Agent Plugin (pluginId, version, archiveDigest, skill names, and exports with component/version/props schema/consent/availability and a ready embed snippet).

catalog.name: plugins_set_enabled
catalog.description: Turns a plugin ON or OFF. This is the ONE tool for enabling and disabling plugins, and it covers BOTH of Tovu's plugin systems — say which with the required 'family' argument: 'agent-plugin' for an Agent Plugin found by search_agent_plugin_local (e.g. the image/video plugin), 'site-runtime' for a .tovu-plugin site plugin listed by content_read.plugin. Use this when the user asks to enable, disable, turn on, turn off, activate or deactivate a plugin, or when a plugin you need is installed but not active. Every enable opens the owner's approval card, including site plugins sealed here with plugin_source_seal. For Agent Plugins the same card lists the external MCP sources, declared tools and may-write grants to turn on; discovery reloads after approval. Disabling is not confirmed. Author site-local behavior with plugin_source_create/open → write/edit → seal → enable (family 'site-runtime'). Site plugins support content filters, content types and fields, plus sdk.routes.add (http.route.register + contributes.routes, mounted under /api/p/<plugin-id>), sdk.tools.add (tools.register + contributes.tools, ids p_<normalized-plugin-id>__<name>), and sdk.widgets.add (render.contribute + contributes.widgets, public SSR partials). Refuses to enable a site-runtime plugin whose discovery status is 'invalid' or 'incompatible'; enabling one with a data module runs live schema DDL (ADR-023) — reversible in the sense that disabling flips the activation flag back, but not a pure no-op toggle. Installing and uninstalling are SEPARATE tools, deliberately: this one only flips an already-installed plugin's switch and its listed access; it never installs or removes plugin packages.

family.description: Which plugin SYSTEM the id belongs to. Required, and never guessed — Tovu has two unrelated systems that share the word 'plugin'. Use 'agent-plugin' for an Agent Plugin (an agent-plugins.org package with a plugin.json, skills and an optional mcp.json — anything search_agent_plugin_local returned, e.g. an image/video plugin). Use 'site-runtime' for a .tovu-plugin site/runtime plugin — anything content_read.plugin returned. If you did not get the id from one of those two tools, call the matching one first rather than picking a family.

pluginId.description: The plugin id. For family 'site-runtime', as returned by content_read.plugin. For family 'agent-plugin', the plugin.json 'name' as returned by search_agent_plugin_local. An id that is not installed/discovered in THIS workspace is refused, and nothing is written.

enabled.description: true to enable, false to disable. ENABLING ALWAYS ASKS THE HUMAN FIRST — this tool opens a confirmation dialog and waits for the answer, because turning a plugin on changes what you yourself can do next; do not promise the user it is on until this call returns with changed:true. Disabling is not confirmed (it only removes capability). For family 'site-runtime', enabling a plugin whose manifest declares a data module runs schema DDL against the live database (ADR-023's snapshot-protected, transactional core-mediated engine) and is refused unless the plugin's discovery status is 'valid'; disabling has no such precondition. For family 'agent-plugin', enabling reports restartRequired:true for the legacy agent_plugin_<id> registration only. Load its guidance now with load_agent_plugin and use agent_plugin_connect if it needs account sign-in. Continue with available tools; do not ask the person to restart Tovu or claim an unavailable tool is ready.

catalog.name: plugins_uninstall
catalog.description: Uninstalls a plugin. This is the ONE tool for uninstalling plugins, and it covers BOTH of Tovu's plugin systems — say which with the required 'family' argument, same as plugins_set_enabled. For family 'site-runtime': moves a site-installed plugin to the Trash (restorable for 60 days from Admin → Trash; only a human can delete it permanently), removing it for all workspaces on this site. Refused if the plugin is a built-in (nothing to remove), or if it is currently enabled in ANY workspace (the on-disk artifact is shared across every workspace this instance serves, so removing it while another workspace still has it enabled would silently break that workspace) — call plugins_set_enabled with enabled:false everywhere it is on first. For family 'agent-plugin': PERMANENTLY removes the Agent Plugin from THIS workspace — its package and activation record. This is NOT reversible from inside Tovu: there is no Trash for this family, and reinstalling means re-running the install with the plugin's archive. Refused if the id is not installed in this workspace or is BUNDLED with Tovu (bundled plugins are re-seeded on every boot) — call plugins_set_enabled with family 'agent-plugin' and enabled false instead. Either way, ALWAYS ASKS THE HUMAN FIRST: this tool opens a confirmation dialog and waits for their answer; nothing is removed unless they confirm, and a cancel or no answer comes back as a result, not an error.

family.description: Which plugin SYSTEM the id belongs to. Required, and never guessed — same rule as plugins_set_enabled's 'family' argument, and the same reason: Tovu has two unrelated systems that share the word 'plugin'. Use 'agent-plugin' for an Agent Plugin (an agent-plugins.org package — anything search_agent_plugin_local returned). Use 'site-runtime' for a .tovu-plugin site/runtime plugin (anything content_read.plugin returned). If you did not get the id from one of those two tools, call the matching one first rather than picking a family.

pluginId.description: The plugin id. For family 'site-runtime', as returned by content_read.plugin — must be a site-installed plugin (a built-in has no on-disk artifact to remove and this is refused). For family 'agent-plugin', the plugin.json 'name' as returned by search_agent_plugin_local — must be installed in this workspace and not bundled with Tovu.

installCatalog.name: plugins_install
installCatalog.description: Installs a SITE plugin (.tovu-plugin, the kind content_read.plugin lists) from a local folder or .zip on the machine Tovu runs on, or a chat ZIP source.attachmentRef (get it from chat_list_pending_attachments). Use when the user asks to install or add a plugin from a folder or zip. The package is inspected and an invalid one is refused before anything is written; the result names its trust tier and carries a warning saying whether it runs code — tell the user. Set replace:true to replace an installed version (refused while that plugin is on). The plugin is installed OFF in every workspace — turn it on afterwards with plugins_set_enabled (family 'site-runtime'). Hosted servers refuse installs without TOVU_PLUGIN_LOCAL_INSTALL=1; desktop and dev sites install directly. To AUTHOR a site plugin use plugin_source_create/open, write/edit files, seal, then enable. Does not install Agent Plugins, themes or skills, and does not download anything.

kind.description: folder for an unpacked package; zip for a local ZIP or chat attachment.

path.description: Absolute path on the machine Tovu runs on. Exactly one of path/attachmentRef.

attachmentRef.description: Opaque attachment:<uuid> for a file on this message: copy it from chat_list_pending_attachments. Not derivable from the file's disk path or folder. ZIP only; exactly one of path/attachmentRef.

replace.description: true to replace an installed version of the same plugin id. Default false.

sourceCatalog.name: plugin_source_create
sourceCatalog.description: Creates a minimal valid site-local tier-3 draft with a manifest, server entry and README. Existing drafts are retained; existing installs are opened without overwrite. Site-local workflow: plugin_source_create (scaffold) or plugin_source_open (latest installed working copy) → list/read/write/edit draft files → plugin_source_seal → plugins_set_enabled (family site-runtime). Drafts never run. Site plugins support content filters, declarative content types and fields. Use sdk.routes.add with capability http.route.register and contributes.routes (e.g. GET /items); routes mount at /api/p/<plugin-id><path> and declare public/member/admin access. Use sdk.tools.add with tools.register and contributes.tools; assistant ids are p_<plugin-id with hyphens replaced by underscores>__<name>. Use sdk.widgets.add with render.contribute and contributes.widgets for public SSR partials. Every registration must match its manifest declaration. Tier-3 runs with full server access; sandboxing is deferred by owner decision.

sourceCatalog.name: plugin_source_seal
sourceCatalog.description: Validates the draft manifest, computes integrity for every package file, uses a higher manifest version or bumps the latest patch on updates, and installs through the existing installer. Keeps active versions plus the newest three for rollback after a successful reload and reloads enabled code through the controlled loader; initially disabled plugins stay OFF. Validation errors explain what to fix. Check installed/reloaded/reloadError. Runs directly on desktop/dev; hosted installs require TOVU_PLUGIN_LOCAL_INSTALL=1. Site-local workflow: plugin_source_create (scaffold) or plugin_source_open (latest installed working copy) → list/read/write/edit draft files → plugin_source_seal → plugins_set_enabled (family site-runtime). Tier-3 runs with full server access; sandboxing is deferred by owner decision.

Preserves active versions, the newest three releases and your unsealed draft. Fails plainly when no previous version exists. If reload quarantined the plugin, enable it after rollback. Site-local workflow: plugin_source_create (scaffold) or plugin_source_open (latest installed working copy) → list/read/write/edit draft files → plugin_source_seal → plugins_set_enabled (family site-runtime). sources.description: Reads content metrics and other data the installed 'Word Count' plugin has already computed and stored for one existing post or page. This post's word count and estimated reading time — computed and stored automatically every time the post is saved while this plugin is enabled. Plugin discovery: tovu/word-count word count reading-time content-metrics. Requires an existing postId — call content_post_search, content_post_list, or content_post_get first if you do not already have one. Returns null for any field this plugin has not written yet for that post (for example, one never saved since 'Word Count' was enabled), plus a note explaining why, rather than failing the call.

fields.description: This post's word count and estimated reading time — computed and stored automatically every time the post is saved while this plugin is enabled.

sources.description: Runs the installed 'Content Analyzer' plugin on one existing post or page right now and returns its fresh result (nothing is saved). Analyze this post's SEO: overall content score 0-100 from title length, meta description length, image alt text, heading order, a single H1, word count and subheadings — recomputed every time the post is saved while this plugin is enabled. Word count of the post's body text (headings excluded), measured by the SEO content analyzer on every save.
